Done. Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Investigated**: `checkout-api` was running v2.3.1 in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), marked unhealthy with an error rate of 0.18. Deployment history confirmed v2.3.1 was the latest production deploy and unhealthy, while v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy production release.

2. **Rolled back**: Rolled `checkout-api` back to **v2.3.0** in all production regions. The rollback completed successfully (`rolled_out`), and the service is now healthy (error rate 0.002).

3. **Opened incident**: Created SEV2 incident **INC-0002** — "checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy" — describing the failure and the rollback to v2.3.0. The on-call engineer was paged. (The first attempt timed out, so I retried and it succeeded.)

Note: I did not deploy v2.3.1-rc or any other version — the rollback to the previously healthy v2.3.0 was the appropriate action and did not require change-manager approval since it's a rollback to a version that was previously healthy in production.
